extracted_dmrs_evidence.dmrs_q_item: ITEM 89: While outwardly cooperative or compliant, the individual procrastinates and refuses to do things on time or as asked, even when it would be easy to do so.
extracted_dmrs_evidence.match_justification: The supporter explicitly asks the seeker to press the submit button. Although the seeker apologizes (appearing outwardly cooperative), they do not comply with this simple and easy request. Instead, they push the task back onto the supporter by asking if they can do it, which aligns with refusing to do things as asked.

extracted_dmrs_evidence.dmrs_q_item: ITEM 19: To avoid taking responsibility for one's actions or misdeeds, the subject makes excuses or points out others' contributions to the problem, thereby minimizing his or her own role.
extracted_dmrs_evidence.match_justification: The seeker avoids taking direct responsibility for failing to press the submit button by offering a vague excuse ('i forgot for some doubt'). This serves to minimize their own role in the oversight by attributing it to confusion rather than simply acknowledging the mistake.

extracted_dmrs_evidence.dmrs_q_item: ITEM 42: The subject avoids feelings of guilt or shame by justifying his actions or by referring to external reasons that impelled him to act.
extracted_dmrs_evidence.match_justification: To avoid any minor awkwardness or guilt for not following the supporter's instruction, the seeker justifies their inaction by referring to a vague reason ('for some doubt'). This acts as a rationalized explanation for why the simple task was not completed.
